content: These technologies are framed as transformative forces driving operational efficiency, cost optimization, and smarter mining practices. The push for modernization in this sector is driven by the need for operational efficiency, safety improvements, and cost reductions. This is particularly relevant for the mining sector, which is inherently cyclical and sensitive to global commodity pricing and supply chain disruptions. Earlier evaluations of the sector highlighted the profound advantages of digitalizing mining operations across the continent, which include significantly improved workforce productivity, optimized cost management, and enhanced environmental outcomes [33] . Automation and artificial intelligence have gained substantial momentum, enabling data-driven, autonomous operations that enhance safety and productivity while simultaneously minimizing operational costs. Furthermore, operational edge control systems, which facilitate the real-time management and optimization of mining activities, are increasingly sought after as companies strive to improve decision-making processes and reduce their environmental impact. South Africa's mining sector continues to benefit from improved commodity prices for key minerals, including chrome, manganese, and platinum, which has driven strong export results and fostered a highly positive economic environment [51] . In April 2026, South African mining production experienced a notable 8.2 percent year-on-year expansion, suggesting robust sectoral growth and operational scaling [55] . These specific applications are heavily cited as primary growth drivers, reinforcing the overarching global trend toward reducing operational costs, minimizing human exposure to hazardous underground environments, and enhancing overall site safety . By leveraging historical and real-time data, predictive models have allowed operators to accurately forecast machinery failures before they occur, thereby minimizing costly unplanned downtime and substantially enhancing workplace safety [Source 3]. Furthermore, the proliferation of autonomous systems, such as driverless haul trucks and robotic drills, gained considerable traction during this timeframe [Source 3]. These autonomous solutions have been instrumental in removing human personnel from hazardous environments, thereby reducing exposure to dangerous conditions while simultaneously maximizing continuous mining productivity [Source 3].
